title: EventConductor events.yaml
description: Event triggers declared outside the workflow definitions, in a file named events.yaml (or events.yml) next to them. Either a list of triggers, or an object whose only key is triggers holding that list. Each entry is a definition's trigger plus the workflow it starts: a domain event (CloudEvents) of the given type arriving on the destination, for which the filter holds, starts a process of that workflow with the business key and variables mapped from the event — while the workflow is ACTIVE and the trigger is not paused. The counterpart of cron.yaml for schedules.

id.description: Optional name of the trigger (letters, digits, '.', '_', '-'), unique within the workflow it starts — across the definition's own triggers and every events.yaml. A pause is kept under <workflow>/<id> and the default business key carries it. Absent means derived from the type (com.acme.booking.created; a second trigger of the same type in the workflow gets -2). An id the definition already declares makes the entry a duplicate: listed, never fires.

destination.description: A logical destination, mapped to a topic by workflow.events.destinations.<name>.topic — the same names PUBLISH_EVENT publishes to, never a topic itself. In kafka mode the engine consumes the topics of the destinations that some trigger or onEvent names; events also arrive through POST /workflow/api/events/{destination}, the publishInboundEvent MCP tool and the embedded InboundEventService.

type.description: The CloudEvents type to match (ce_type), e.g. com.acme.booking.created. '*' matches any run of characters (com.acme.booking.*); a lone '*' matches every event on the destination, including plain records that carry no type (a CDC topic, for instance).

workflow.description: The id of the workflow definition a matching event starts. An entry naming an unknown workflow is reported and skipped.

filter.description: Optional JEXL boolean expression over the event, without ${...} (e.g. data.op == 'u' && data.after.active). The event is used only when it evaluates to true; an expression that cannot be evaluated counts as false and is recorded as an ERROR receipt. Evaluated over the event context: id, source, type, subject, time, key, destination, datacontenttype, data (the payload parsed as JSON — objects are maps, so data.after.id — or its raw text) and extensions.

businessKey.description: Optional text template over the event for the started process's business key (e.g. "customer-${data.after.id}"). Absent means <workflow>-evt-<trigger>-<16 hex of a SHA-256 of the event's source and id>, so a redelivered event collapses into the process it already started. A given key is honoured as given: two different events that render the same key start one process.

variables.description: The started process's initial variables, by name, each a payload template over the event ("${data.after.id}"; a non-string value becomes its JSON text, as process variables are strings). Absent means every top-level member of data when data is a JSON object; {} means none.
